title: Decision Orchestrator — trace & scoring contract for multi-region routing
content:
Purpose:
This note captures a proposed runtime contract and internal design for the Decision Orchestrator (the component that evaluates routing policies, constraint checks, and scoring used to decide model variants and regional routing). The goal is to define:
- a compact, stable explainability log schema for downstream auditing and ML-eval correlation;
- the scoring and constraint-check phases with deterministic ordering and idempotency;
- control-plane API shapes for rollout managers and multi-region failover;
- practical sampling, retention, and privacy controls for logs.

Audience and scope:
Primary audience: platform engineers, runtime owners, SRE, and applied-ML teams who consume explainability traces for model quality regressions and audits.
Scope: runtime-level decision evaluation for per-request routing (not model training or long-running batch re-ranking). Covers hosted and Dedicated modes and how we annotate decisions for Private deployments (where some fields may be redacted).

Design principles:
- Deterministic evaluation ordering: constraints (hard denies) run before soft scoring so we can short-circuit and make fallbacks immediately auditable.
- Minimal stable trace: logs must be compact, schema-stable, and easily queryable by token (request id) and time.
- Privacy-first: sensitive fields are either hashed or omitted depending on deployment flags.
- Non-invasive metrics: scoring should not add appreciable P95 latency — prefer cached pre-evals where possible.
- Versioned contracts: decision logs include evaluator version and policy bundle id for repro.

Glossary (brief):
- Decision Orchestrator: runtime module that applies constraints, scores alternatives, and emits the final routing decision.
- Candidate: a routing target (model variant, region, or fallback tier).
- Constraint: boolean check (deny/allow) that rules out candidates.
- Score: numeric (float) assigned to remaining candidates for ranking.
- Explainability log (xlog): compact artifact capturing inputs, intermediate results, and final decision per request.

High-level flow (per request):
1) Normalize input (tokenize/metadata extraction).
2) Candidate generation: from policy rules and model catalog; include pinned candidates if present.
3) Constraint evaluation (fast, fail-fast): each constraint emits a result and reason if denied. If all candidates denied, go to fallback policy.
4) Feature enrichment: lightweight features for scoring (latency_estimate, cost_estimate, recent_error_rate). Where possible pull from cache.
5) Scoring pass: produce scores for each candidate; apply score transforms (penalties, exploration bonus).
6) Selection + tie-breakers: deterministic tie-breaker (candidate id hash + request id seed).
7) Emit explainability log and signal control plane of any stateful changes (metrics, counters, sample traces).

Constraint evaluation details:
- Constraints must be pure functions of request context + candidate metadata (no side effects). That allows deterministic replays during offline analysis.
- Each constraint has: id, severity (hard/soft), evaluation_cost_estimate (ms), and description.
- Hard constraints = immediate exclusion. Soft constraints feed into scoring as penalties.
- Ordering: inexpensive checks (region compatibility, SLA tier) run first; expensive checks (model-compatibility heuristics that touch profiling db) are deferred or cached.
- Shortcut semantics: if a hard constraint removes all candidates, the orchestrator attempts configured fallbacks in order (regional fallback, model-family fallback, degrade-to-hosted-low-priority). Fallbacks are recorded in the xlog with reasons.

Scoring design:
- Score = base_score(candidate) + sum(neg_penalties) + exploration_noise. Base_score is often derived from historical success_rate and throughput profile for the model variant.
- Score normalization: all scores mapped to [-1.0, 1.0] for consistency across evaluation versions.
- Deterministic pseudo-randomness: exploration_noise uses HMAC(request_id, evaluator_version) to ensure reproducible exploration seeds.
- Weight configuration comes from policy bundle; weight changes are part of rollout semantics (see control-plane section).

Explainability log (xlog) schema (flat, column-friendly):
Fields (all strings or numbers):
- xlog_id: unique id (uuid4)
- request_id: request-level id
- timestamp: ISO8601 UTC
- evaluator_version: semver
- policy_bundle_id: string
- routing_context_hash: short-hash (redactable)
- candidates: pipe-separated list of candidate ids (e.g., us-east-m-7b|us-west-m-7b|dedicated-1)
- constraints_passed: pipe-separated list of constraint ids that passed
- constraints_failed: pipe-separated list of constraint:id:reason (colon-delimited)
- scores: pipe-separated list of candidate_id=score (numeric, 3-decimals)
- selected_candidate: candidate_id
- selection_reason: enum (top_score|fallback|pinned|tie_breaker)
- latency_estimate_ms: integer
- cost_estimate_cents: integer (per 1k tokens scaled)
- sampling_flag: enum(full|sampled|none)
- redaction_mode: enum(none, hash, drop)
- region_hint: original request region if present
- privacy_tags: pipe-separated tags (e.g., pii, personal_data)
- extra_notes: short free text (max 512 chars)

Notes on schema choices:
- We avoid deep JSON in xlogs to keep ingestion and SQL analytics fast. Pipe-separated fields are easy to explode in our ingestion pipeline.
- All candidate lists keep stable ordering as evaluated; the scores field matches that ordering for easy join.
- Provide a lightweight constraints_failed field with colon-separated reason to speed triage.

Sampling & retention:
- Default sampling: 0.1% full xlogs, 5% scored-only traces (scores + selected candidate), always capture full xlog on errors and on canary traffic buckets.
- Retention: full xlogs retained 90 days; scored-only traces 365 days; aggregated metrics indefinite.
- Private deployments: default redaction_mode is hash; tenant can request drop for specific fields via config.

Control-plane contracts and APIs:
- EvaluateDecision(request_context) -> DecisionResponse (sync call for low-latency path). DecisionResponse contains selected_candidate, reason, evaluator_version, and xlog_id (if sampled). For private deployments we also support EvaluateDecisionAsync when external policy lookup required.
- PolicyBundle Deploy: bundle_id, evaluator_version, change_set (weights, constraints delta), rollout_plan (percentages and regions), expires_at. Runtime must be able to atomically swap bundle id per rollout step.
- Rollback semantics: control-plane exposes Rollback(bundle_id, reason) and the orchestrator should prefer prior stable bundle atomically. Rollouts are staged: per-region percentage, then global.
- Audit API: GetXlog(xlog_id) returns the stored xlog; GetDecisionHistory(request_id) returns recent evals for same request_id. Access is gated by roles and tenant permissions.

Multi-region considerations:
- Data locality: region_hint should be used to prefer local candidates to minimize P95. However, policy rules can override locality for cost/performance tradeoffs.
- Stale catalogs: orchestrator must include model-variant timestamps; if candidate metadata is older than threshold, treat as lower confidence (score penalty).
- Cross-region fallbacks: prefer warm-standby models in adjacent region before cold-start remote. Track cold-start penalty in scoring so decisions are reproducible.
- Failover coordination: when a region reports degraded capacity, control-plane broadcasts a temporary constraint (region_capacity_ok=false) which the orchestrator evaluates immediately. Change must be idempotent and time-bounded.

Telemetry and metrics (critical for SRE):
- Per-evaluator metrics: eval_latency_ms (p50/p95/p99), constraints_evaluated_count, avg_candidates_per_request, fallback_rate, xlog_sample_rate.
- Per-candidate metrics: assign_count, avg_success_rate, avg_latency_observed.
- Alerting: fallback_rate > 1% sustained (5m) triggers ops review. Rapid rollout-induced fallback spikes should auto-suppress rollouts until investigated.

Operational notes and rollout plan for new evaluator version:
- Canary (1% requests in single region) with xlog full capture. Monitor fallback_rate and latency delta.
- Slow ramp to 10% across regions over 24h, maintain sampling and add targeted debug samples for failing customers.
- If fallback_rate or client-visible error increases > threshold, rollback automatically.

Privacy and compliance:
- PII policy: any field marked privacy_tags includes a mapping to redaction rules. By default, request payloads are hashed and source tokens are not stored in xlogs.
- For regulated tenants, provide option to store only scored-only traces and to forward full xlogs to customer-owned storage in Private deployments.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- How much of candidate generation should live in control-plane vs runtime? (current tilt: candidate generation is runtime-local for latency, but control-plane provides hints).
- Should we switch to columnar JSON for xlogs (one JSON per candidate) to improve extensibility? That trades off ingestion complexity.
- Where to store long-lived per-candidate profiles (throughput/success_rate)? DB vs in-memory materialized view.

Next steps / action items:
- Finalize xlog schema and get sign-off from SRE and compliance (owner: Maya Patel, due 2024-03-22).
- Implement a lightweight EvaluateDecision RPC prototype with deterministic seed for exploration (owner: Jordan Lee, due 2024-04-05).
- Add sampling knobs to runtime config and surface rollout controls in console backend (owner: Sofia Alvarez, due 2024-04-15).

Appendix: example xlog line (pipe-separated)
xlog_id|request_id|timestamp|evaluator_version|policy_bundle_id|routing_context_hash|candidates|constraints_passed|constraints_failed|scores|selected_candidate|selection_reason|latency_estimate_ms|cost_estimate_cents|sampling_flag|redaction_mode|region_hint|privacy_tags|extra_notes
123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000|req-20240301-42|2024-03-01T18:22:31Z|v1.3.0|bundle-2024-02-28|ahf9c3|us-east-7b|region_ok,quota_ok|model_blacklist:region_restricted|us-east-7b=0.812|us-east-7b|top_score|12|5|full|hash|us-east|none|pinned-by-route

References and related tickets:
- Confluence: Decision Orchestrator Overview (linked above)
- Jira: PLAT-4893 (policy rollout automation), PLAT-5021 (xlog ingestion schema)
- GitHub: PR 2112 (prototype: deterministic-seed-exploration)

End of note.
